assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED made strong, controllable coupling of a superconducting artificial atom to a single microwave photon a practical architecture: dispersive readout, qubit-qubit coupling via resonators, and the basis of most present superconducting processors. The concept is original, clear and has had very broad impact on both quantum information and microwave quantum optics. I judge this as a field specialist and would apply extra scrutiny because of that.
assessment.attribution: The theory proposal (Blais and collaborators) and the first strong-coupling experiment (Wallraff, Schoelkopf and colleagues) are naturally split between theory and experiment. A three-person prize of Blais, Wallraff and Schoelkopf is defensible, but the 2004 proposal and experiment had additional co-authors who are not in the supplied credit, and I cannot independently verify the relative contributions.
assessment.maturity: Two decades of independent confirmation across many laboratories and platforms; the interpretation is stable. Timing needs care because the 2025 prize recognized macroscopic quantum effects in superconducting circuits; this is a distinct and later conceptual step, but the committee should weigh how close the two awards are.
uncertainties: Overlap in subject area with the 2025 prize may be viewed as too close in time.
Credited names omit some co-authors of the foundational proposal and experiment.
Possible perceived conflict through my own work in superconducting circuits and QED; no specific relationship is asserted.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock, built on the magic-wavelength trapping idea, delivers fractional uncertainties near 1e-18 and underpins the prospect of redefining the second, tests of fundamental constants and relativistic geodesy. It is an invention with clear, measurable and lasting impact.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed and first demonstrated the magic-wavelength lattice clock concept; Ye's group drove it to the extreme precision regime and developed key enabling technology. Two laureates is a clean configuration, although others contributed to strontium and ytterbium lattice clocks and to comb-laser stabilization; I cannot adjudicate those claims fully.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature: multiple groups worldwide reproduce and surpass the performance, and international timekeeping bodies are moving toward a redefinition. Recognition is timely and not premature.
uncertainties: Other contributors to lattice clock development and to laser stabilization may be thought to deserve credit.
The 2005 prize covered frequency combs, so the committee may debate overlap in precision-metrology territory.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: BB84 and the entanglement-based protocol established information-theoretic secure key distribution grounded in quantum mechanics, a conceptually original and widely recognized idea that connects foundations to technology. Impact on quantum communication, networks and cryptography research has been large.
assessment.attribution: Bennett and Brassard introduced BB84, and Ekert introduced the entanglement-based protocol in 1991. These are the natural three names and they fit a prize configuration. Alternatives such as the related teleportation work are listed under a separate ballot entry that I do not rank, to avoid duplication.
assessment.maturity: Experimental demonstrations, satellite links and commercial systems are well established, though real-world security depends on implementation details and the scientific core is theoretical. The 2022 prize addressed Bell-inequality experiments and quantum information science, so the committee may judge whether this is sufficiently distinct.
uncertainties: Relation to the 2022 prize on entangled photons and quantum information science.
Whether the theory-led nature fits physics rather than computer science or mathematics.
Practical security gaps are a separate issue from the original discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The 1995 proposal for trapped-ion quantum gates and the later proposals for quantum simulation with cold atoms provided the theoretical blueprint for two leading quantum technology platforms. The originality and breadth are very high, and the proposals were concrete enough to be built.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller are the clear intellectual authors of both proposals, so a two-person prize is a natural fit. Experimental realization belongs to others (for example on ions), which might call for a separate or combined configuration, but the supplied credit here is limited to the two theorists.
assessment.maturity: Experiments in ion traps, neutral atoms and Rydberg arrays have repeatedly confirmed the proposals. The 2012 prize recognized ion manipulation, so some overlap exists, but the theory contribution is distinct and mature.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2012 prize (Wineland, Haroche) on controlling single quantum systems.
Compound entry combining two themes; one might be preferred over the other.
A related ballot entry credits Rainer Blatt for the experimental side.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Bringing macroscopic mechanical oscillators into the quantum regime (ground-state cooling, entanglement, squeezing and quantum state transfer) tests quantum mechanics at large mass scales and enables quantum transducers and sensing. The work spans optical and microwave circuit implementations, which I find especially interesting from a circuit-QED viewpoint.
assessment.attribution: Cleland (quantum ground state and single-phonon control in a piezoelectric resonator), Teufel (microwave circuit sideband cooling and squeezing) and Aspelmeyer (cavity optomechanics, entanglement and large-mass tests) are distinct contributors. The topic is a compound discovery and others, such as groups credited in the early cooling and cavity optomechanics work, may have equal claim; I am not certain of the full story.
assessment.maturity: Strong and independent experimental confirmation exists across several platforms, but the field is still evolving and the end applications are not yet clear. Recognition would be somewhat early compared with other candidates.
uncertainties: Several groups have comparable contributions, so a three-name selection may be contested.
Adjacent to my own field and to the 2025 prize, so I should avoid giving it extra weight.
Long-term impact on technology is still developing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect and the Z2 topological insulator, followed by the observation in HgTe quantum wells, opened a large field of topological band physics with strong conceptual originality and wide influence on condensed matter research.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the theoretical prediction, and Molenkamp's group delivered the first experimental observation, although Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang proposed the HgTe route and are not in the supplied credit. This is an important unresolved attribution issue that I cannot settle from the information given.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed in many materials and followed by 3D topological insulators and applications in spintronics and topological quantum computation concepts. The field is mature, although technological impact is limited so far.
uncertainties: The supplied credit omits the proposers of the HgTe realization.
Competing claims over three-dimensional topological insulators and related earlier work (for example by Fu, Kane, Mele and by Zhang and collaborators) complicate allocation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The proposal for spin qubits in quantum dots, and its experimental realization with coherent control and high-fidelity operations in silicon, defined a leading route to scalable semiconductor quantum computing compatible with existing manufacturing. Originality and importance are considerable.
assessment.attribution: Loss and DiVincenzo made the 1998 proposal; Vandersypen's group has led much of the single- and two-qubit experimental demonstration, but other experimental groups (Kouwenhoven, Marcus, Tarucha, Morello, Dzurak and others) made key contributions. Three laureates cannot capture all of them.
assessment.maturity: Rapid progress and independent confirmation exist, but the platform has not yet demonstrated the scale to settle its eventual role in quantum computing; recognition may be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Many experimental contributors beyond the supplied names.
Eventual technological position relative to superconducting and atomic platforms is unclear.
Relation to my own field means I should not overweight quantum-computing hardware.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Atom interferometry makes matter-wave interference a precision tool for gravimetry, inertial sensing, measurements of fundamental constants and tests of the equivalence principle, with a clear lasting scientific and instrumental impact.
assessment.attribution: Bordé, Pritchard and Kasevich are commonly cited for foundational concepts and demonstrations, but Chu, Mlynek, Kasevich and Pritchard and others overlapped, and I cannot resolve the relative priority from supplied information. The credit set is plausible yet may be incomplete.
assessment.maturity: The methods are mature, with gravimeters in operation and ongoing long-baseline experiments, though the headline fundamental tests are not yet decisive. Recognition is timely, since the technique is established and the 1997 cooling prize did not address interferometry.
uncertainties: Attribution among groups is contested and partly outside my own knowledge.
Overlap with the 1997 and 2001 prizes in laser cooling and condensate physics.
